title: A stranger can call capture_guest_rsvp straight over the public API and fill an event with made-up guests, because its only rate limit lives in the app.

source.ref: SCAN-1224 review of the anon-callable SECURITY DEFINER functions, 2026-11-16 (security thread, requested by Daniel). Confidence: PLAUSIBLE (read from the live function body; not exercised).

detail:
EVIDENCE: public.capture_guest_rsvp(uuid,text,text,uuid) is SECURITY DEFINER and granted to anon. It validates the email shape and the event's state, then inserts an event_rsvps row with status 'going'; enforce_event_rsvp_capacity demotes to waitlist when full. The only throttle is rateLimitOk in app/(main)/events/guest-rsvp-actions.ts, which a caller using the public anon key against PostgREST never passes through. An event id is public on any event page.

WHY IT MATTERS: A script can take every seat of a public free event with generated addresses (real guests then land on the waitlist), and can write junk emails into the host's roster. No data leaks; the damage is capacity and roster pollution.

FIX DIRECTION: Revoke execute on capture_guest_rsvp from anon and call it from the server action with the service-role client (the action already rate-limits per IP and per event), or add a DB-side limit (a per-event hourly cap on guest rows created by this function). Apply as a migration through the normal gated path; the same move is the template for the other write functions in the review.

2026-11-16: migration 20270346063000 is written and NOT yet applied. It puts a cap inside capture_guest_rsvp: at most 60 new guest seats per event per rolling hour and 300 per rolling 24 hours, refused with the same receipt and logged; an address that already holds a seat is never counted. Signature and grants are unchanged, so every caller works as before. This bounds roster pollution; it does not stop a room smaller than 60 being filled in one burst, which still needs the grant moved off anon and the action calling with the service role. Stays open until the migration is applied and the cap is seen in production.

verify.evidence: Open: anon still holds EXECUTE on capture_guest_rsvp. Close when has_function_privilege('anon', 'public.capture_guest_rsvp(uuid,text,text,uuid)', 'EXECUTE') is false and the guest RSVP action still works, or a DB-side cap is in place.
